title: 第一卷 第5章 丽妃拉拢
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

一名宫女将一方丝帕覆在丽妃腕上，叶笙歌屏息凝神，三指轻轻搭上寸关尺。指尖下的脉搏跳动急促而有力，但深处又有一丝涩意。

“娘娘可否让奴才观一观舌苔？”

丽妃瞥了他一眼，略有些不耐，但还是依言微微张口。

舌质红，苔薄黄而干。

“娘娘近日是否常觉心中烦热，尤以午后及夜间为甚，口干欲饮，但饮不解渴，手足心热，睡眠不安，易生口疮？”叶笙歌收回手，垂目问道。

丽妃漫不经心的神色收敛了些，瞥了他一眼：“有点意思，继续说。”

“且娘娘虽觉内热，却又畏风，不喜贪凉，偶有咽痒微咳，痰少而黏，可是如此？”

丽妃坐直了身体，目光落在叶笙歌低垂的头顶：“你倒真有两下子。太医只说本宫肝火旺，开了些清火的方子，吃了总不见好，反觉胃脘不适。你说，这是何故？”

叶笙歌沉吟片刻，谨慎答道：“回娘娘，依奴才浅见，娘娘此症，并非寻常实火，而是‘火郁内灼’之证。”

“外似有寒，实则内热久郁，不得宣发。热郁于内，煎灼阴液，故见五心烦热、口干舌燥；郁热熏蒸，上扰心神，则眠差易怒。”

“然此火为郁火，清泻苦寒之药，易伤脾胃，反使气机更滞，郁热更深，故而无效，甚或加重。”

他顿了顿，补充道：“此证与婉贵妃娘娘的虚寒内侵、阳气不振之体，恰好相反。”

丽妃听完，盯着他看了好一会儿，忽然笑了起来，笑声却没什么温度：“好，说得好。看来你不是瞎猫碰上死耗子。那你说，该如何治？”

“此症首重疏解郁热，宣畅气机，而非一味清泻。用药当以轻清宣透为主，佐以养阴，缓缓图之，并需调畅情志，忌食辛辣厚味、温补之品。”叶笙歌斟酌着字句。

“情志？”丽妃嗤笑一声，眼神却冷了下来，“在这宫里，你让本宫如何调畅情志？”

“罢了，既然你能看出症结，想必也有些手段。你便来替本宫推拿疏导一番，若能让本宫此刻舒坦些，本宫重重有赏。”

不容叶笙歌拒绝，她已重新倚回榻上，微微阖眼，一副等待伺候的模样。

叶笙歌无法，只能硬着头皮上前。

他净了手，回想方才脉象与舌苔，判断郁热壅滞之处主要在肝经与胸胁。他伸出手指，隔着衣物，精准按压她肋下某处穴位。

Page (1/3)

A palace maid put a silk handkerchief on Concubine Li's wrist. Ye Shengge held her breath and concentrated, and gently placed three fingers on the inch-guarantee ruler.The pulse under the fingertips beat rapidly and powerfully, but there was a hint of astringency deep down.

"Can your Majesty allow me to take a look at the coating on my tongue?"

Li Fei glanced at him, a little impatient, but she still followed the words and opened her mouth slightly.

The tongue is red and the fur is thin, yellow and dry.

"Have you often felt hot and bothered recently, especially in the afternoon and night? Your mouth is dry and you want to drink, but drinking does not quench your thirst. Your palms and soles are hot, your sleep is restless, and you are prone to aphthous sores?" Ye Shengge withdrew his hand and lowered his eyes and asked.

Li Fei's careless expression calmed down a bit, and she glanced at him: "It's interesting, keep talking."

"Although the empress feels internal heat, she is afraid of wind and does not like cold. She occasionally has an itchy throat and a slight cough, with less and sticky phlegm. Is this so?"

Concubine Li sat up straight, her eyes falling on Ye Shengge's lowered head: "You really have a problem. The imperial doctor only said that I have a strong liver fire, so he prescribed some prescriptions to clear the fire, but it didn't feel better after taking it. Instead, I felt epigastric discomfort. What do you think is the reason for this?"

Ye Shengge pondered for a moment and replied cautiously: "Returning to Madam, according to my humble opinion, Madam's disease is not an ordinary excessive fire, but a sign of 'fire stagnation and internal burning'."

"It seems to be cold on the outside, but in reality the internal heat is stagnant for a long time and cannot be released. The heat is trapped inside and burns the yin fluid, so you can see five palpitations and heat, dry mouth and tongue; the stagnant heat is fumigated and disturbs the mind, resulting in poor sleep and irritability."

"However, this fire is stagnant fire. Medicines used to clear away bitter cold can easily damage the spleen and stomach. On the contrary, they will make Qi more stagnant and stagnant heat deeper, so they will be ineffective or even aggravate."

He paused and added: "This syndrome is exactly the opposite of Concubine Wan Guifei's body of internal deficiencies and coldness and lack of yang energy."

After hearing this, Li Fei stared at him for a while, then suddenly laughed, but the laughter was not warm: "Okay, that's good. It seems that you are not a blind cat who just met a dead mouse. So, how should I treat it?"

"The first priority of this disease is to relieve the stagnation of heat and relieve qi, rather than blindly clearing and purging. The medicine should be mainly light and clear, supplemented by nourishing yin, slowly and slowly, and it is also necessary to regulate emotions and avoid eating spicy, thick, and warming foods." Ye Shengge considered the words.

"Emotions?" Concubine Li sneered, but her eyes turned cold, "In this palace, how do you ask me to regulate my emotions?"

"Well, since you can see the crux, you must have some means. Come and give me some massage and counseling. If you can make me feel more comfortable at this moment, I will be rewarded."

Not allowing Ye Shengge to refuse, she leaned back on the couch again, closed her eyes slightly, and looked like she was waiting to be served.

Ye Shengge had no choice but to step forward.

He cleaned his hands, recalled his pulse and tongue coating, and judged that the main areas of stagnation due to stagnation of heat were the liver meridian and chest and hypochondrium.He stretched out his fingers and pressed an acupuncture point under her ribs accurately through her clothes.
